ad_library.summary: 1 live Meta ad confirmed on 2026-11-21 on the ManasaEnterprises page (page ID 1259997940531140), running since 22 Aug 2026 and clicking to WhatsApp. It is the only ad in this batch that publishes a full price ladder - 3 kW Rs.2,05,000, 5 kW Rs.3,10,000, 10 kW Rs.5,92,000 - plus a Rs.78,000 subsidy claim, two phone numbers, an email and two cities. Every price and the subsidy carry an asterisk with no footnote in the ad. No website is linked and manasaaenterprises.com did not load, so no site audit was run.

funnel.meaning: The ad publishes a full three-tier price ladder and then sends every click to a WhatsApp chat with no landing page behind it. A buyer who has just been shown a Rs.5.92 lakh price has nowhere to check the company, the asterisk's conditions or the warranty, and the business cannot retarget or measure the click.

findings: Every price in the ad - 3 kW Rs.2,05,000, 5 kW Rs.3,10,000, 10 kW Rs.5,92,000 - and the Rs.78,000 subsidy figure carry an asterisk, and no footnote, T&C or qualifying condition appears anywhere in the ad. On a Rs.5.9 lakh quote the terms are the offer.

The prices are quoted per kW size with no panel brand, inverter brand, module wattage, structure type or warranty term attached to any of them, so the three tiers cannot be compared with each other or with any competitor's quote.

The ad claims 'GOVT. SUBSIDY UP TO Rs.78,000' but the three system prices are not stated as net or gross of it, so a buyer cannot tell whether the Rs.2,05,000 for 3 kW already has the subsidy in it - and at 3 kW the subsidy is the single largest line item in the purchase.
There is no website: manasaaenterprises.com did not load on 2026-11-21, and every click ends in a WhatsApp chat, so a buyer cannot verify the distributor before committing to a lakh-scale order.
The business calls itself a 'SOLAR MASTER DISTRIBUTOR' and the ad runs in Hyderabad, but the only address detail in it is 'Kakinada | Hyderabad' - no area, no street, no pin code for either city.

Only third-party corroboration of an address exists (Justdial lists Miyapur, behind RBR1 Complex, Hanuman Temple Road, 4 years in business), and the ad itself carries none of it - nor a single review, install count or project photograph.
The single ad has been running unchanged since 22 Aug 2026 with no variants, so there is no message test in the account and no evidence any creative angle has ever been tried.
next_steps: State, in the ad, whether each price is net or gross of the Rs.78,000, what the asterisk conditions are, and what is included (panel/inverter brand, structure, net-metering, warranty). It is the cheapest credibility upgrade available and it costs one line of copy.
Attach a specification to each of the three tiers
3 kW / 5 kW / 10 kW with a panel brand, an inverter brand and a warranty term turns three numbers into three comparable products - and is what a buyer needs to shortlist against another quote.
Put up one page, even a single page

The ad already publishes the hardest content to write (a price ladder). A one-page site repeating it with the address, the asterisk, the warranty split and a Meta Pixel would make every click measurable and retargetable - and give the buyer somewhere to check the firm.
Say where in Hyderabad you actually are
'Kakinada | Hyderabad' is not an address. The Justdial listing gives Miyapur, behind RBR1 Complex, Hanuman Temple Road - publish it, with a map link, in the ad and on the page.

A named install, a kW size, a locality and a photograph. A 'master distributor' claim on a lakh-scale purchase with no install, review or project behind it is the weakest part of an otherwise unusually-specific ad.

One ad unchanged since 22 Aug 2026 means the account has never learned anything. A variant leading with the 3 kW price and one leading with the subsidy would answer which hook this market responds to.

site_evidence.note: This business has no website that loads, so no pixel or UTM check was possible. Recorded as not checked rather than absent. The ad lands on a WhatsApp chat, which carries no campaign parameters.

promise_gap.site: The asterisk has no footnote anywhere in the ad and there is no website where the conditions could be read. Whether the price is net or gross of the Rs.78,000 is never stated.
No ad or page explains who applies for the subsidy, when it is credited, or what the buyer pays before it arrives.
No manufacturer authorisation, brand list or dealer certificate is named anywhere - and the ad names no panel or inverter brand at all.
